Same symptom here on Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, but a different mechanism, worth ruling out before assuming it's the `drop_eagle_block` path.

**Discriminator:** re-run with `--no-async-scheduling`, nothing else changed. If corruption goes to zero while your hit rate stays put, it isn't the cache-read path, block dropping is unaffected by async scheduling.

Ours: 16/288 with async scheduling, 0/288 without, 0/288 with prefix caching but no MTP. It's a host/device race, the accepted-token counts are copied D2H in step N's row order, `_update_states` permutes that same pinned buffer in step N+1 before anything waits on the event, and the `prev_positions` gather then permutes them again, so a request picks up another request's count. Patch: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53919

Your title update says this persists in v0.28.0 — worth knowing that #50729 ("[Bugfix][Mamba] Fix overlapping state copy race", member-authored, merged to main Aug 17) **missed the 0.28.0 branch cut**, so v0.28.0 does not contain it. Neither does v0.27.1.

That fix addresses a speculative-decode **conv-state shift copying within the same physical block with overlapping source/destination ranges** — parallel memcpy-style loads/stores give no memmove ordering, so the shifted window can read partially-overwritten state. That is mechanically very close to the wrong-conv-window / GDN-snapshot corruption this issue tracks, and it would naturally correlate with prefix-cache hit rate (hits are what re-enter conv state mid-stream).

Suggestion: re-run your 288-request repro on a build that contains #50729 (the `v0.28.1rc0` tag or current main), async scheduling ON, everything else identical. If it drops to 0/288, this cluster has a root-cause candidate; if not, that's an important negative that rules the copy race out. Sibling fixes in the same lineage worth having in the build: #53077 (GDN empty-draft-schedule count reset) and #54076 (align-mode chunk splitting uses the Mamba cache group's block size).

Thank you @erdholion !
I managed to check fix #50729 and it solves the issue.
Is there a minor release including this fix expected, or will it be included in 0.29.0?

Glad it's confirmed! To answer the release question: #50729's merge commit (`a02cfccb`) is an ancestor of the `v0.28.1rc0` tag, so the fix ships in **v0.28.1** — no need to wait for 0.29.0. Until it's stable, the rc0 tag or current main are the fix-containing options.
Is there any information about when 0.28.1 will be released?

We're hitting this too, on a configuration this thread hasn't covered yet — different GPU vendor, different quantization scheme, low concurrency — so it looks like independent corroboration rather than a duplicate.

**Environment**

- vLLM **0.27.1** (pip-installed, verified via `python -c "import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)"`)
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet/Mamba architecture, **INT8 W8A16** (compressed-tensors), MTP speculative-decoding head baked into the checkpoint
- Hardware: **2× RTX 3090 (Ampere), tensor-parallel-size 2** — not H100/MI355 like the other reports in this thread
- KV cache dtype: `fp8_e4m3`
- Relevant server flags:
  ```
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --disable-custom-all-reduce
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 170000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype auto
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 16
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
  --watermark 0.02
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
  ```
  Async scheduling is not explicitly disabled anywhere in our launch command — i.e. we run in the state @johny-jose's discriminator (`--no-async-scheduling`) flags as the corrupting one.
- Low concurrency: `max_num_seqs=4`, single internal router in front, nothing like the 24–32-way GUI-agent traffic in the OP or PR #53919's repro. Worth noting since it shows this isn't purely a high-concurrency phenomenon.

**Observed**

On 2026-08-31, ~18:15–19:24 CEST, the server degenerated into a sustained bad window (not an isolated flaky response): every request that hit the prefix cache came back as either endless repeated CJK characters or empty content, `finish_reason` still reported `stop`, no crash, no 5xx. The window included trivially short prompts — a plain "reply with just OK" request came back as an endless CJK stream, so this isn't confined to long shared-prefix agent traces; a cache hit alone was enough to trigger it. Root-caused live to `--enable-prefix-caching` + MTP against this issue; we swapped to a non-MTP preset to recover, then re-tested.

**Mitigation test**

Same model/hardware, `--enable-prefix-caching` disabled, MTP left on, everything else identical. 30 requests across four blocks (10× short deterministic prompt, 10× long mixed prompt, 5× identical prompt repeated back-to-back — the historical cache-trigger path, 5× multi-sentence coherence check): 0/30 corrupted, no CJK, no repetition loops, no unexplained empty content. That isolates prefix-caching (not MTP alone) as the trigger on our build, consistent with this issue's title.

**On the "fixed" state of this issue**

We've since re-enabled `--enable-prefix-caching` (informed, accepted risk — restart-on-corruption is an acceptable fallback for us right now), so we're intentionally running the failure mode described here in production and can gather more data on request.

Given the thread: PR #50729 does not apply to us (confirmed absent from both v0.28.0 and our installed v0.27.1, per @erdholion above), so it isn't a candidate explanation for what we saw. What does line up with our config — prefix caching + MTP + async scheduling not disabled — is the mechanism @johny-jose isolated, whose fix (#53919) is still open and unmerged. We haven't yet run the `--no-async-scheduling` discriminator ourselves to confirm which of the two open mechanisms (cache-read block-dropping vs. the host/device count race) explains our case — happy to if that's useful data for this thread — but wanted to flag before this gets closed on the strength of #50729 alone: that PR addresses a third, separate race, and #53919's mechanism is, on the evidence in this thread, still unresolved and still open.

**Questions**

- Is there a timeline for merging #53919?
- Any update on when v0.28.1 (containing #50729) actually ships as a stable release?
- Given three distinct races have now surfaced under this one symptom (cache-read block-dropping, memcpy/conv-state overlap, host/device count permutation), would it be useful for us to run the `--no-async-scheduling` isolation test here and report back, to help separate which of the still-open mechanisms is live in our config?

@karls0r — on whether the `--no-async-scheduling` isolation test is worth running: yes, and it's a cleaner discriminator than it looks, because we're both on v0.27.1 and the gate is static there.

The gather that #51571 identifies as the defect sits inside an `if self.use_async_scheduling` branch. In v0.27.1, `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2118`:

```python
    if self.use_async_scheduling and prev_req_id_to_index:
        prev_idx = self.prev_positions.np[:num_reqs]
        ...
    else:
        # Non-async mode: use values directly
```

So `--no-async-scheduling` doesn't merely make the race less likely on your box — it removes the code path that #53919 patches. #51571's own fix plan says as much in its step 5 ("Preserve current upstream InputBatch ownership for non-async scheduling"). That makes @johny-jose's discriminator sound on your exact build: the cache-read block-drop path is scheduler-independent (`MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` accepts `drop_eagle_block` but never acts on it in v0.27.1, and `kv_cache_coordinator.py:755` skips the eagle margin entirely for `MambaSpec`), so if corruption survives async-off it is not #53919's mechanism.

Two controls worth keeping when you run it, since a null is only meaningful if the exposure is unchanged:

1. Confirm your `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` rate is the same in both arms. Async-off changes step timing, and if the hit rate moves you've changed exposure, not mechanism.
2. #53919's own repro only shows the bug under host starvation — its test plan notes that without `--cpus`, an idle box reads 0-1/192 and the bug looks absent. At `--max-num-seqs 4` you may be under the detection floor in *both* arms, so budget enough requests that the async-on arm actually produces a nonzero count before reading anything into an async-off zero.

I don't have a useful arm to contribute here: our v0.27.1 hybrid-GDN + MTP k=3 + prefix-caching box runs `--no-async-scheduling` at low concurrency, so per the gate above the #53919 path never executes on it, and a null there is uninformative by construction.

@rdlh Thanks — first 0.27.1 datapoint in the thread. Two config details would make it considerably more useful, since they discriminate between mechanisms:

1. **Was async scheduling enabled?** On 0.27.1 with `"method": "mtp"`, async scheduling defaults to **on** unless you passed `--no-async-scheduling` (the `None` default resolves in `vllm/config/vllm.py`, and MTP is in `EagleModelTypes`, so it doesn't hit the disable branch). As noted above, the #51571 path is statically gated on async scheduling in 0.27.1 — so if your 12/5000 arm ran with async on, the result is consistent with that known mechanism; if it ran with async off, it's evidence of an async-independent path, which would matter to everyone using `--no-async-scheduling` as a mitigation.
2. **What effective concurrency?** #35288 reports corruption at `--max-num-seqs 4` that disappears at 2, so in-flight request count affects reproducibility.

And yes, please share the repro script. If it's easy to vary, one shape worth including: prompt length just under a block boundary with enough `max_tokens` that the boundary lands mid-decode — cached blocks then contain decode-written state, which prompt-only-block shapes never exercise.

One data point that may or may not be your case: on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next we traced "a small fraction of responses degenerate with MTP on" to a strided `state_indices_tensor_p[:, 0]` view (the Mamba block table is `1 + num_speculative_blocks` wide once speculation is configured) read with unit stride by a state-carrying kernel, so every prefill after batch row 0 in a prefill-only scheduler step wrote its state into request 0's checkpoint blocks — #55357 has the reproducer and mechanism, #55375 the fix for the PLE short conv (the merge candidate; my duplicate #55467 is closed). The tell is that the corruption needs two or more prompts prefilled in the same step and disappears when they arrive 150 ms apart, independent of prefix caching. If your fraction tracks concurrent arrivals rather than cache hits, it is worth checking the state-index consumers of the GDN path in your build for the same assumption.

Thanks for the continued triage here — we have a repro that discriminates against a generic decode-vs-prefill drift explanation and is consistent with rejected-draft contamination of the cached state.

**Config:** Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (hybrid GDN), dflash K=7, `mamba_cache_mode=align`, prefix caching on, `disable_eagle_block_drop=true` (the #53388 opt-out; we enabled it after measuring a warm-throughput win in an A/B), v0.28.1rc1.dev642. Block size 1648.

**Repro (needs a server with this model and config):**
1. Prompt = 500 seeded random 7-digit numbers (seed 101 or 202), then generate with `guided_regex="[0-9]{7}( [0-9]{7})*"`, `max_tokens=2400` (returned 2400 chars). Random arm: `temperature=1.0` → logged draft acceptance 3.6–4.2%. Countdown arm: `temperature=0` → the model emits a descending sequence the drafter predicts; logged acceptance 88.7%.
2. Follow-up = prefix + first 470 space-separated groups of the generated region. Both arms measured the same cached-hit boundary (`cached_tokens=4944` vs prompt `3999` — one block boundary, 945 tokens, beyond the original prompt, covering generated/decode-written content).
3. Compare greedy 20-token continuations: 5 cache-read requests (B) vs 3 cache-skipped references (R; `prompt_logprobs=1`, which returned `cached=0` in all reference runs).

**Result:** countdown arm — B and R produced identical 20-token continuations, 0/5 divergent. Random arm — 5/5 divergent (B and R each self-consistent). A separate truncation sweep keeping 0/235/470 groups (approximate doses; measured `(prompt, cached)` = `(3999, 3296)`, `(5872, 4944)`, `(7600, 6592)`) gave 0/5 → 5/5 → 5/5. One earlier trial pair was also fully clean at low acceptance, so not every such hit diverges.

**Source observation (deployed wheel):** with the opt-out, `use_eagle_block_drop()` is False, disabling both the read-side trailing-block drop and the write-side `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` shift; separately, `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` does not use its `drop_eagle_block` parameter in either lookup branch in this build (per this issue's report this also affects the default path — we only exercised the opt-out path live). As a hypothesis for inspection, not a validated fix: making the Mamba finder honor the drop may need care to keep read-side dropping aligned with checkpoint handling across both lookup branches.

Sanitized repro script: https://gist.github.com/Suppressor72/8a8090d45c15e0a034079403ad8e6dcd (env vars: `VLLM_BASE`, `VLLM_MODEL`, `VLLM_API_KEY`; optional `VLLM_LOG` for acceptance-rate tailing).

Follow-up with validation results and a fix-design caution. Scope note up front: our result is for **DFlash2 speculative decoding in the no-identifiable-draft-group fallback** (the configuration from our earlier comment); it does not establish a fix for the reporter's MTP configuration or for the identified-draft-group path, and the default-path bug as originally reported may still need a real fix.

**Removing the opt-out restored the expected cache boundary in our reproducer.** With `disable_eagle_block_drop` removed (default restored), the same test now measures the cache-hit boundary stopping short of the drafted region (4944→3296 cached tokens against a 3999-token prompt). In one high-margin probe, cache-read and cache-skipped continuations matched exactly on that context. The low-acceptance arm still records digit-level divergence between cached-read and reference requests, but its character changed: pre-fix, cached-read outputs were stable and identical across repeats within a side (one run: 8/8 identical) while consistently disagreeing with the reference; post-fix, the residual differences vary run to run across repeats. That behavior is consistent with harmless numerical variation between a partial and a full recompute, though the cause remains unproven — we have not done a logit-margin or state-level check.

**Caution on the obvious fix:** we drafted the minimal "honor `drop_eagle_block` in both `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` lookup branches" patch (decrement the search bound by one unit when the flag is set — one hash unit in the fine-grained path, one block in the coarse path) and, on source review, found three reasons this candidate is unsafe to propose as a fix:

1. When a draft KV group *is* identifiable, the grouping code deliberately leaves Mamba groups unmarked, so Mamba receives `drop_eagle_block=False` and the patch is a no-op in that configuration.
2. In the flag-all fallback (our configuration — no draft group identifiable), it can double-drop if full attention has already reduced the shared candidate by one unit by the time Mamba is queried, so Mamba's additional decrement can skip below the checkpoint the write-side shift deliberately saved.
3. With hash units smaller than Mamba blocks, a one-unit decrement can still return the same physical state block (`fine_idx // scale_factor` unchanged) — the returned hit is not provably separate from the poisoned one.

A robust fix likely needs to follow the actual state-block and copy-on-write lifetime rather than decrementing the lookup bound.

Validated config for the above: same model/wheel as our earlier comment; only change = `disable_eagle_block_drop` removed from `speculative_config`.

**Field observation: cross-request content exposure on GLM-5.3-Flash (hybrid Mamba, MTP-3, `mamba_cache_mode=align`) — an MTP datapoint, and a symptom class distinct from output degeneration**

Posting as a field report, not a reproducer — we cannot reproduce on demand, every synthetic attempt came out clean. Two reasons it may be useful here: (a) the symptom we observed was not loops or word salad but *content leaking across requests*, verified string-by-string; (b) it is an MTP-configuration datapoint alongside @Suppressor72's DFlash2 no-identifiable-draft-group result, which explicitly did not cover MTP.

**Setup**
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash, W4A16 (AWQ) — hybrid Mamba/GDN + sparse-MLA indexer.
- Engine: `wtdcode/vllm-backport` v0.13.1 (fork base = upstream main `93911fcf`, 2026-09-10). Stock vLLM cannot serve this model on our hardware (sm80 has no sparse-MLA backend — all candidates rejected at startup), so the fork is our only path; the code involved is inherited from upstream, not fork-authored. The same behaviour is present in the official `v0.30.0` tag: `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` declares `drop_eagle_block` and never acts on it, and the hybrid coordinator still skips the eagle margin for `MambaSpec` ("its finder never drops").
- Hardware: 4× A800 (sm80), TP4 + EP, gpu-memory-utilization 0.94.
- Serving flags of interest: `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, `--max-num-seqs 4`, `--block-size 256`, `--max-model-len 524288`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, prefix caching enabled.
- Discriminators you would ask about first, so here they are: **async scheduling was left at its default**, i.e. enabled (MTP qualifies, mp executor supports it); **`mamba_cache_mode` resolved to `align` by default** under prefix caching for this model (`config.py:625` line in our logs). So this report is *consistent with* the async-gated path discussed above — we are not offering it as an async-independent datapoint.
- Traffic: several concurrent long-lived agent sessions, mixed client applications, contexts 57K–226K tokens, prefix-cache hit rates 97–99% on the affected sessions.

**Observation (2026-09-24)**
Two concurrently active sessions received assistant messages whose reasoning text contained strings that appear nowhere in the request. We keep full request/response traces and checked string-by-string that the leaked material exists only on the response side: (i) an opaque session identifier belonging to a different client application; (ii) a Windows filesystem path from that other client's host. Separately, a 226K-token session dissociated: its reasoning restated the user's request correctly while the visible answer claimed it had received no content and hallucinated a prior assistant turn that never existed. A related anomaly (a truncated tool-call JSON) had occurred ~24 h earlier on the previous engine process.

**Controls**
- Same conversation history replayed against a hosted GLM-5.3-Flash endpoint: fully normal.
- The recorded polluted request replayed verbatim to the same engine: clean — consistent with load / hit-rate dependence.
- Synthetic canary: 4 concurrent requests sharing a planted 20K prefix with unique opaque markers, victims expected to hit at high rate, 3 rounds: 12/12 clean. The failure only appears under real multi-session load shapes.
- Server journal for the window: zero errors, zero preemptions, zero repetition detections, normal speculative acceptance rates — silent by construction.
- Application layer excluded: the edge hop is a stateless pass-through (audited), and our tool-call-repair patch is inert on the affected calls.
- Structural isolation: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (pure attention MLA, no recurrent state) behind the same client stack and canary: 27/27 clean across a month of production load.

**Why this points at the path in this thread**
For content absent from the request to appear in a response, the model must have attended to state the request never produced. The only mechanism in this configuration that can hand a request someone else's recurrent state is the Mamba checkpoint / prefix-cache reuse path, and we sit exactly at that intersection: hybrid Mamba + prefix caching + spec ≥ 2, victims at 97–99% hit rate. With MTP-3 the rejection stream is continuous, so a trailing checkpoint over unverified positions stays reachable and a later request can resume from it.
Stated plainly: this is elimination-based inference, not a proven causal chain. But even setting attribution aside, one request must not be able to expose another request's content, so we read it as correctness-critical rather than a tuning tradeoff.
One extra fact for the coordination question: our fork does **not** carry the manager-side drop — commit `a47f0f82` reverted the earlier port of #48375 on the grounds that the coordinator's replay-boundary retention already covers this case. Our observation is hard to square with that reading, which is part of why we are raising it upstream as well.

**Questions**
1) Is the decode-written-state case considered blocking for #57128 to land? If helpful, we can attach the redacted request/response excerpts showing the leaked strings absent from the request, plus the canary design we used.
2) If you would rather track cross-request exposure as its own symptom, say so and we will open a dedicated issue instead of extending this one.

Record on the fork, same evidence chain with code-level localization: `wtdcode/vllm-backport#107`.

@ming616 One concrete mechanism that produces this symptom class, if your GLM-5.3 build runs RecoverSSM (compact KDA recovery; `--use-replayssm` upstream): in align mode, when a speculative window's accepted tokens end exactly on a recurrent block boundary, the commit plan and the postprocess kernel select the *next* block-table column for the committed state (`n // block` instead of `(n - 1) // block`):

- [`kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py#L285-L288`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24c9772d19251dbbf70fef75119546827c540c63/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py#L285-L288)
- [`v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py#L95-L99`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/24c9772d19251dbbf70fef75119546827c540c63/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py#L95-L99)

That column can still be unallocated, so the commit is dropped while the running-state column is advanced to it. The next step reads whatever that page last held, which after a free can be another request's state, and a prefix-cache hit at that boundary reuses it. Nothing logs an error and acceptance looks normal; long contexts make it more likely because more boundaries are crossed.

Fix and test: [local-inference-lab/vllm@a02f585d](https://github.com/local-inference-lab/vllm/commit/a02f585d3f2418cb9f9e8d70c9229bb179b5f86c) (Martin Vit). The same change is in #58863 ([5567cc1b25](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58863/commits/5567cc1b25c6fe79b99d228068017e371efc2570)), where it also covers the Qwen GDN path; on our GB10 build (main 1ea7c63f4 + that PR) the fork's test fails 3 of its boundary cases without the fix and passes with it.

Does your fork pass `--use-replayssm` (or enable compact KDA recovery by default)? If not, this is not your path.

I reproduced the W4A16/XPU hybrid MTP + prefix-cache output corruption on an Arc Pro B70. The notable part is that some cold requests fail with **zero prefix-cache hits**, so a fix limited to dropping the last *matched* cache block may not cover this case.

Controlled probe on a cached XPU fork (`exl3xpu:pinned-21412bdd`, image ID `sha256:77785c51423fe49a0c4a097d78e9b1bf03ae17f0076e2f39d43d85071d854c17`): vLLM `0.26.1.dev0+g568afb3a1.d20260907`, torch `2.12.0+xpu`, Qwen3.8-derived AutoRound W4A16 compressed-tensors model. Single B70 (`ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0`), BF16 compute, FP8 KV, eager mode/XPU graphs off, context 16,384, `max-num-seqs=1`, batched tokens 4,096. The MTP cells used `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4}'`. Each cell had a fresh server. I sent three identical short HTML coding prompts, then three identical long versions with a repeated ~4K-token prefix, serially, with `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, 3,072 output tokens, and thinking disabled. All responses returned normally; I inspected full saved text rather than treating a missing `<script>` at the output cap as a failure.

- Cache ON, MTP OFF: **6/6 coherent** capped HTML outputs. The two warm long requests each registered 4,096 prefix-cache hits.
- Cache OFF, MTP4 ON: **6/6 coherent** capped HTML outputs.
- Cache ON, MTP4 ON: **5/6 visibly corrupted** (mixed-language fragments, repeated delimiters/`</think>` and gibberish). The two corrupted short requests and the corrupted cold long request registered **zero** cache hits; the two warm long requests each registered 2,048 hits and also corrupted.
- Cache ON, MTP4 ON, plus `--no-async-scheduling`: **5/6 visibly corrupted**, including three cold/zero-hit requests; warm long requests registered 2,048 hits each. Async scheduling was not required for this reproduction.

The cache+MTP combination changes the path even before the first reuse. It also halves the hit count for the long prompt (2,048 versus 4,096 without MTP). A prior run on a different, pinned vLLM `0.27.2rc1.dev77+gac7509e2b` XPU stack saw 8/9 long outputs degenerate with cache ON/MTP4 and coherent output with cache OFF/MTP4, but that run did not preserve all raw texts; I am not conflating it with the controlled fork probe above.

For now, disabling prefix caching when serving this W4A16 model with MTP4 is the verified mitigation on this machine. I have not isolated the source-level cause. This may be in the MTP/cache scheduling or GDN speculative state path, not only the warm-cache block-boundary condition in #48375.

**Gap in the patch as proposed.** The `max_num_blocks -= 1` lands on the coarse branch, but on 0.29.0 `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` returns earlier whenever fine-grained hashing is active:

```python
if alignment_tokens < block_size and block_size % alignment_tokens == 0:
    hash_block_size = alignment_tokens
    scale_factor = block_size // hash_block_size
    max_num_partial_units = min(max_length // hash_block_size, len(block_hashes))
    for fine_idx in range(max_num_partial_units - 1, -1, -1):
        ...
        return computed_blocks, hit_length          # returns here

max_num_blocks = max_length // block_size          # the patched line
if use_eagle ...: max_num_blocks -= 1               # unreachable in that config
```

`alignment_tokens` is `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens`, i.e. `hash_block_size` for exactly the configs that `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` classifies as `has_partial_mamba_group` (mamba page > hash block). So any deployment using `--prefix-match-unit` below the mamba page size — which is how you get fine-grained partial hits at all — bypasses the fix entirely. It looks like the same one-unit back-off is needed on `max_num_partial_units` in that branch.

Two smaller notes from reading 0.29.0: the parameter is named `drop_eagle_block` there (not `use_eagle`), and `kv_cache_coordinator.py` still carries the "No margin for mamba: its finder never drops" comment while passing `drop_eagle_block` down, so caller and manager still disagree about who is responsible.

Follow-up: I implemented the fine-grained half and ran it on the box this is reported from.

**Diff against 0.29.0** (`MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit`; the parameter is named `drop_eagle_block` there):

```python
         block_size = kv_cache_spec.block_size
         if alignment_tokens < block_size and block_size % alignment_tokens == 0:
             ...
             max_num_partial_units = min(
                 max_length // hash_block_size, len(block_hashes)
             )
+            if drop_eagle_block and max_num_partial_units > 0:
+                max_num_partial_units -= 1
             for fine_idx in range(max_num_partial_units - 1, -1, -1):
                 ...
             return computed_blocks, hit_length

         max_num_blocks = max_length // block_size
+        if drop_eagle_block and max_num_blocks > 0:
+            max_num_blocks -= 1
```

Both branches now back off exactly one *search unit* — a hash block in fine-grained mode, a cache block otherwise. That is the same unit `FullAttentionManager` uses (`hit_length -= min(alignment_tokens, block_size)`), except that a mamba block list cannot be trimmed after the match the way append-only attention KV can, so the range has to be shortened before the search instead of the result after it. The coarse hunk is #43650 verbatim; the fine hunk is the part that lands below its `return`.

**What the fix is aimed at, observed.** Instrumenting the finder on this config (hybrid GDN 27B, mamba page 2176 tokens, `--prefix-match-unit 128`, so `block_size=2176`, `alignment_tokens=128`, fine path taken):

```
[mamba-hit-probe] block_size=2176 align=128 max_length=86656 max_units=677
                  drop_eagle=True fine_idx=676 hit=86656 blk_aligned=False
```

`drop_eagle_block=True` does reach the mamba manager, and the match is a **partial tail** entry — `_cache_partial_tail_block` registers one at `floor(prompt_len / 128) * 128`, i.e. at the prompt's last hash boundary, which is the generation point — returned while `FullAttentionManager` refuses the equivalent position.

**Cost, measured on a replay of a real 87k-token agent session** (six consecutive steps, same prompts, patch on vs off):

| step | cached before | cached after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 78,336 | 78,336 | 0 |
| 3 | 86,656 | 78,336 | −8,320 |
| 4 | 87,040 | 87,040 | 0 |
| 5 | 87,040 | 86,784 | −256 |
| 6 | 91,392 | 91,392 | 0 |

Four of six unchanged; worst case is 9.5% of the prompt. That worst case is amplified by sparse retention — with `retention_interval = 13056` the next older *retained* mamba snapshot can be a whole segment back; with dense checkpointing the tail loss should be bounded by one mamba block. Worth knowing before choosing the back-off unit if you have a view on whether a hash block is enough vs. a whole mamba page.

**Status.** Two hunks, applies to 0.29.0 at `--fuzz 0`. The prefix-reuse correctness probe (cold prefill vs. cache hit, greedy, 4.2k / 10.6k / 16.9k / 25.4k) is still token-identical, and the replay run is clean — but note that replaying the whole 18-step request sequence that produced the corruption never reproduced it even unpatched, so this is a correctness argument against the code path, not a reproducer.

Two things, because your Q2 refers to a hunk I posted in this thread and I need to retract it before anyone builds on it.

## The fine-grained hunk in my 2026-09-29 comment is withdrawn — it was wrong

@TyroneNel reviewed it as #245 and ran this project's own mamba/EAGLE/hybrid prefix-cache tests against our post-series tree:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| post-series, **without** the hunk | 93 passed / 0 failed |
| post-series, **with** the hunk | 84 passed / **9 failed** |

including a sibling hit going 1536 → 0. The mamba search bound is *already* one drop unit below the attention hit before the hunk runs — the coordinator's *"No margin for mamba"* rule, plus `FullAttentionManager` doing its own `hit_length -= min(alignment_tokens, block_size)`. Passing that already-reduced `max_length` into the mamba finder is what protects the boundary; my hunk subtracted a second unit and discarded correct hits.

My probe line, `max_length=86656 ... hit=86656`, I presented as "the state lands on the generation point". That is the normal case — `hit == max_length` means the bound handed in was already the reduced one. I read it backwards, so that comment's evidence is not evidence. The PR is closed and the hunk is out of our tree.

## Your questions

**Q2.** `disable_eagle_block_drop: true` and `drop_eagle_block` are opposite directions, and the hunk keyed on the latter being true — so with drop disabled it would not have fired at all. Moot now, but the question underneath it is the right one: not "does the drop apply" but "does the default bound already keep the mamba state off the generation point". On the test results above, it does.

**Q1.** I would not dismiss it, but note what the withdrawal implies: if keeping the trailing partial block were sufficient on its own to corrupt a continuation, the post-series tree *without* the hunk would not pass those tests. That is a prefix-cache unit test and not your 0.5M-token agentic session, so it does not settle it — but it does mean the mechanism is not as direct as my hunk assumed.

**Q3.** An A/B on a **replay of the real session** is the right shape, since you have already shown synthetic traffic does not reproduce it. The arms I would trust, in order:

1. `disable_eagle_block_drop: true` vs `false`, same replay, same seed, greedy — compare the output **token for token**, not "did the sentence appear". If your recipe samples, the comparison needs the same seed *and* the same sampler path to mean anything.
2. MTP off, same replay — that separates "MTP is the ingredient" from "heavy prefix reuse is the ingredient".
3. Instrument the mamba finder to log the matched boundary per request (`max_length`, `hit_length`, whether the matched block is a partial tail). If the boundary is byte-identical in both arms, the flag is not the lever and the search should move elsewhere; if it differs and the text differs with it, you have a much stronger claim than either of us has now.

The probe in that 09-29 comment does work — it is the interpretation that was wrong, not the measurement. I can send it as a standalone 0.29 patch that only logs, no behaviour change, if that is useful to you.

One caveat worth stating: our symptom is punctuation soup (`!` repeated), and you are explicit that yours is not. Nothing I have is evidence that they are the same bug rather than two things that live in the same config class. If the boundary turns out identical in your A/B, that would be the first real evidence that your path is a separate one.
